stemMd: Under the Italian Constitution, how is the President of the Republic chosen, and for how long?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Elected by Parliament in joint session, joined by delegates of the Regions, for five years

options.label: B
options.textMd: Elected by Parliament in joint session, joined by delegates of the Regions, for life

options.label: C
options.textMd: Elected by Parliament in joint session, joined by delegates of the Regions, for seven years

options.label: D
options.textMd: Elected directly by the voters, for seven years

options.label: E
options.textMd: Elected directly by the voters, for five years

explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** Each choice pairs a method of election with a length of term, so both halves have to be right.

**The facts that settle it.** In Italy the voters do not elect the head of state. Article 83 of the Constitution provides that the President is elected by Parliament in a joint session of its members, joined by three delegates from each Region chosen by its regional council (Valle d'Aosta sends one). Article 85 sets the term at seven years.

**How to check it.** Compare the term with the other numbers in the Constitution that it is easily confused with. The two chambers are elected for five years (Article 60), so a seven-year presidency is longer than a legislature. Former Presidents become senators for life (Article 59), but that is what happens after the term, not the term itself.

distractorRationale.a: The method is right but the term is borrowed from the chambers: the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate are elected for five years (Article 60). The President's term under Article 85 is seven years, longer than a legislature.
distractorRationale.b: This confuses the presidency with what follows it. Under Article 59 a former President of the Republic becomes a senator for life, but the presidential term itself lasts seven years.
distractorRationale.d: The seven-year term is right, but voters do not elect the Italian President. Some republics, France among them, elect their president by popular vote; in Italy the electorate is Parliament with the regional delegates (Article 83).
distractorRationale.e: This describes the French presidency, elected by popular vote for five years since 2002. It is wrong on both counts for Italy: election by Parliament with regional delegates, for seven years.

accessibilityText: Question: under the Italian Constitution, how is the President of the Republic chosen, and for how long? The choices are: elected by Parliament in joint session, joined by delegates of the Regions, for five years; the same body for life; the same body for seven years; elected directly by the voters for seven years; and elected directly by the voters for five years.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank for the TIL-A History and general knowledge section. The choices cross two electorates with three terms; each wrong term comes from a real constitutional number it is confused with (the five-year legislature, the life senatorship of former Presidents), and the wrong electorate from the French model of a popularly elected president.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Under Articles 83 and 85, Parliament in joint session plus three delegates per Region (one for Valle d'Aosta) elects the President for a seven-year term. Only C combines the right body with the right term. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-reading-gk-run1) reached the same answer: Art. 83 has the President elected by Parliament in joint session, joined by three delegates per Region (one for Valle d'Aosta). Art. 85 sets the term at seven years. A and B get the term wrong, and D and E get the method wrong.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: Article 83 (Parliament in joint session with three delegates per Region, one for Valle d'Aosta) and Article 85 (seven-year term) are both needed; only one choice has both. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
